lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Allocated ninety seconds per visitor. I have never once used them, so take as long as you like.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Callum Strand. Founder of Meridian, signatory to the Handover, and, the plaque says, a steward of the public interest. The plaque is two hundred years old and has been re-cast eleven times.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: People started leaving things. Wire flowers, handwriting, a drawing of a machine with a face on it. I am supposed to clear them nightly and I have stopped.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: It came down and nothing was allocated to put it back up. That is how you know what a thing is actually worth here: not what they build, what they bother to repair.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: The founding documents are behind glass and there is a gap in them. Nineteen months in 2064 with nothing catalogued. I have filed about it four times.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: The gap in the founding documents filled itself last quarter. Eleven senators, four firms and a holding company, all catalogued, all sourced to a public record I have never been able to find.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Provenance, they call that. The record of who owned a thing and when. It is most of my job and almost none of this building.
